si_4_title.answer: Using normative modelling to detect disease progression in mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease in a cross-sectional multi-cohort study

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used an adversarial autoencoder (AAE) to learn the normative model. The AAE architecture included an encoder and decoder with two hidden layers each, and a discriminator. It was conditioned on demographic variables.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: In this paper, we developed the normative model using the adversarial autoencoder (AAE)... In our analyses, we used a conditioned AAE.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Pinaya2021.pdf.md: Normative model / paragraph 1; Normative model training / paragraph 2

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The model used cortical volumes (68 regions), subcortical volumes (including hippocampus, amygdala, etc.), ventricular/CSF volumes, and corpus callosum morphology measures (posterior, mid-posterior, central, mid-anterior, anterior).
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: The final data included the cortical volume for each of the 68 cortical subregions (34 per hemisphere) and the volume of 33 neuroanatomical structures, totalling 101 subregions/ structures... (the complete list is presented in the supplementary materials).
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Pinaya2021.pdf.md: MRI processing / paragraph 1; 41598_2021_95098_MOESM1_ESM.pdf.md: 1. List of brain features

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative model was conditioned on age and sex. Age was transformed into a one-hot encoding vector (27 positions for ages 47-73). Sex was also one-hot encoded.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: In our analyses, we used a conditioned AAE. This type of autoencoder allows us to influence the model's reconstruction using the demographic variables, i.e. age and sex.
